question: How do will, swiftness, shining, and firmness become air, fire, and earth?
premises: Will itself reaches the state of supreme bliss.
Through its association with swiftness it is called air.
Through shining and firmness it appears as fire and earth.
inference: Thus the same will-power differentiates into air, fire, and earth according to its modes.
uncertainties: The compound vahnirbhāsanātsthairyato is compressed; the distribution of bhāsanāt to fire and sthairyataḥ to earth follows the traditional reading.
plain_english: Will itself, having reached supreme bliss, is called air when joined with swiftness; through shining it becomes fire, and through firmness it becomes earth.
